title: Rupa Goswami's Bhakti Rasamrita Sindhu opening
hook: nobody reads an ocean front to back: a book of devotion built in waves
carry: Rupa Goswami's Bhakti Rasamrita Sindhu opening
tomorrow: before the swim, a chart. what does devotion's map hold?

segments.voice: Yesterday, bhakti at the Charitamrita's close: love that holds on while it misses. Today the student from Prayag, Rupa, writes a book of his own, and it's an ocean.

Nobody reads an ocean front to back. You wade in, and the waves come to you. One Hindu book is built that way on purpose. Its parts are called the eastern side, the southern, the western and the northern, and each side is divided into waves. Not chapters. Waves. Rupa Goswami, who once sat by the rivers at Prayag learning about a seed and a creeper, has written a whole ocean. Why waves? Because of one word in the title.
screen: `NOBODY READS AN OCEAN FRONT TO BACK.` → `NOT CHAPTERS. WAVES.` → `ONE WORD IN THE TITLE.`

segments.voice: Take the name a piece at a time. Bhakti, devotion. Rasa, taste, the flavor of a thing. Amrita, nectar. Sindhu, ocean. The ocean of the nectar of devotion's taste. The surprising word is rasa. Sanskrit poets and dramatists used it for the taste a scene leaves in its audience: the flavor of love, or grief, or wonder. Rupa borrows it for devotion. So this isn't only a book about what a devotee should do. It's about what devotion tastes like, and a taste comes in waves, not in steps. The first verse praises Krishna, in paraphrase, as the very form of the nectar of every taste. The next bows to Chaitanya, by whose prompting in his heart, Rupa says, he writes at all. A neighbor tradition reaches for the same sense. In the King James Bible, Psalm thirty-four says: “O taste and see that the LORD is good: blessed is the man that trusteth in him.” Shared: faith as something tasted, known from the inside, not only learned about. And an honest difference. The psalm's taste is God's goodness, trusted in. Rupa's rasa opens into a whole map of flavors, love as a servant, a friend, a parent, a beloved, with Krishna at the center of every one.
screen: `RASA: TASTE, THE FLAVOR OF A THING.` · `DEVOTION, TASTED IN WAVES.` · `O TASTE AND SEE: PSALM 34.` · then, large: `FAITH, KNOWN FROM THE INSIDE.`

segments.voice: If there's something small to eat or drink near you, a sip of tea, a raisin, a piece of fruit, take it slowly and let the taste arrive like a wave: rising, full, then fading. If there's nothing, notice the taste already in your mouth. Then rest at the shore, breathing.
Rupa Goswami's Bhakti Rasamrita Sindhu: the ocean of the nectar of devotion's taste. A book of waves.
